title: Avoid radar charts, whose shapes change with the order of their spokes.
rule: Leave radar charts out of every Oath & Action piece. Draw the same measures as grouped bars from one zero line, a dot plot on one scale, or small-multiple bars with one panel per group, so each value is read as a length from zero or a position.
use_when: Never: a reader who asks how several groups compare across the same measures gets a truer answer from a dot plot or small-multiple bars.

use_instead.when: Each group has one value on each of several measures and the reader compares positions
The reader compares each group’s mix of measures, panel by panel
The reader compares two to four groups within each measure

text: A radar chart draws values as a shape, and a shape’s area grows with the square of its values, so a group a little ahead on every spoke looks far bigger. Moving one spoke to another place changes every shape on the chart with no change in the data, and overlapping outlines hide each other.
why.basis: Design judgment, from the chart system our founder and editor approved in November 2026

builders: No form: the kit draws no radar chart. The sketch, work/build/guide/specimens/s-14-24-sketch.html, draws the radar twice with its spokes in two orders beside grouped bars of the same values; build the better choice with the grouped-bar, dot-plot or small-multiple-bars form.
sketch_alt: Two radar charts draw the same illustrative values for two groups with their spokes in different orders, and the dark group’s shape is the larger in the first and the smaller in the second. Beside them, grouped bars of the same values show the dark group ahead on two measures and behind on three.
